generalizedRange: Atlantic coast of southwest Morocco (wild); reintroduced flocks in the northern Alpine foothills of Germany and Austria and in Andalusia, Spain; a semi-wild colony in southeast Türkiye
hook: Extinct in Europe for 400 years. Now it follows a microlight home.

story.text: A glossy black ibis with a bare red face, a ragged crest, and a long curved bill for probing soil for worms and larvae.
Gessner drew it in 1557; within a century it was gone from central Europe — hunted, nestlings taken, the Little Ice Age hastening the end.
By 1997 the only truly wild population, on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, was down to 59 breeding pairs; guarded, it reached 147 pairs and 708 birds by 2018.
A relict colony of seven, found near Palmyra in 2002, still wintered in Ethiopia; its last bird vanished in 2013, and the east’s wild migration with it.
In 2018 the IUCN moved the species from Critically Endangered to Endangered, a downlisting some researchers call premature.
North of the Alps, human foster parents raise zoo-hatched chicks, then fly ahead of them in a microlight to teach a route no wild elder can.
Warming autumns made the Alpine crossing harder, so in 2024 the plane led 36 juveniles 2,600 kilometres from Bavaria to Andalusia.
They joined Proyecto Eremita’s resident flock: 695 zoo-bred birds released since 2004, 47 breeding pairs in 2025.
To witness the northern bald ibis is to watch a small plane climb with thirty birds strung out behind it — 280 now in Europe, short of the 357 that could stand alone.

stats.size: Up to 30 in (75 cm) long · about 3 lbs (1.3 kg)
stats.lifespan: About 30 years in human care; wild lifespan not well documented
stats.diet: Tactile forager — earthworms, insect larvae & other invertebrates; lizards in Morocco
stats.populationEstimate: About 700 wild birds in Morocco (708 counted in 2018)
stats.populationAsOf: 2018 · per Oryx (Böhm, Bowden & Seddon, Souss-Massa census)

reproduction.text: Colonial cliff-nesters, seasonally monogamous: up to four greenish eggs, incubated 27–28 days from the first egg so chicks hatch about two days apart, and both parents share the rearing until fledging at 42 to 50 days.

insight.text: Each ibis’s bald red head carries its own pattern of black markings, and each has a voice its flock — and its keepers — can tell from every other.

programs.title: LIFE Northern Bald Ibis
programs.summary: Hand-raises zoo-hatched chicks with human foster parents, leads them south behind a microlight each autumn, GPS-tracks the flock, and secures power poles and anti-poaching enforcement toward a self-sustaining Alpine population by 2028.

programs.title: Proyecto Eremita, La Janda
programs.summary: Releases zoo-bred ibises into Cádiz province — 695 birds since 2004 — and monitors three cliff and tower colonies where 319 chicks have hatched wild since 2008, aiming at a resident, self-sufficient Andalusian population.
